Choose the real-time forecasting rule by out-of-sample accuracy

Source: R/measure.R
ec_forecast_select.Rd

Compares candidate forecasting rules on a set of earlier option lives: for each interval, every rule forecasts the clock from data available at the interval's start, and the forecast is compared with the clock that subsequently materialized over the interval. The rule with the lowest root-mean-square error wins. Because the intervals end before the options you want to study, the choice never looks at the test sample — the no-look-ahead discipline of the accompanying working paper.

Usage

ec_forecast_select(
  x,
  intervals,
  rules = ec_forecast_rules(days = c(3, 5, 7, 10, 14, 20), expanding = TRUE),
  realized_method = "rv",
  interval = NULL,
  common = TRUE,
  trunc_sd = ec_default_params()$trunc_sd,
  scale_fn = stats::mad,
  clip = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'ec_forecast_select'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An event_prices object (or coercible).

intervals

A data.frame with columns start and end (valuation time and expiry of each earlier option life), of the same time type as x (or Date bounds for a POSIXct series).

rules

Candidate rules from ec_forecast_rules().

realized_method

Estimator for the realized clock over each interval (default "rv").

interval

Optional staggered sampling interval in minutes, used for both forecasts and realized clocks (intraday data only).

common

Logical; if TRUE (default), score all rules on the intervals where every rule produces a forecast, so the comparison is like for like.

trunc_sd

Numeric, truncation threshold in robust standard deviations (default 3).

scale_fn

Function computing the robust scale of the increments for truncated (default stats::mad()).

clip

Numeric length-2 clipping bounds for q before the log-odds transform; defaults to the bounds stored in x.

...

Unused (for the print method).

Value

An object of class ec_forecast_select: a list with

scores

tibble per rule: rule, type, window, method, n (intervals scored), rmse, mae, bias (mean forecast minus realized), sorted by rmse.

best

the winning row of scores.

detail

long tibble: interval, rule, forecast, realized.

Methods (by generic)

  • print(ec_forecast_select): Print method.

Examples

data(us2016)
ep <- as_event_prices(us2016, time = "date", price = "trump")
# two-week option lives starting every day, all ending before Oct 10
starts <- seq(as.Date("2016-06-01"), as.Date("2016-09-25"), by = "day")
iv <- data.frame(start = starts, end = starts + 14)
sel <- ec_forecast_select(ep, iv,
  rules = ec_forecast_rules(obs = c(21, 41, 61)))
sel
#> -- Real-time clock forecast selection (117 option lives scored)
#> Best rule: trailing 61 obs / rv (RMSE 0.04052)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   rule                     n   rmse    mae      bias
#>   <chr>                <int>  <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 trailing 61 obs / rv   117 0.0405 0.0315 -0.000658
#> 2 trailing 41 obs / rv   117 0.0417 0.0311 -0.00279 
#> 3 trailing 21 obs / rv   117 0.0483 0.0393 -0.00422
